summary: Feed s118_double is degraded: 21.6% of TCP sessions are one-way (exceeds 10% threshold) and 90.7% of bytes are encrypted (exceeds 90% NDR tolerance). NDR requires bidirectional, full-payload visibility - both faults reduce detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is delivering only one direction of bidirectional flows to this NDR port. Most likely asymmetric routing where client->server and server->client traverse different TAP/SPAN points and are not aggregated to the same tool port, or SPAN is configured for Tx-only/Rx-only, or flow-hash load-balancing is splitting directions across tools.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions to reassemble TCP, track state and detect intrusions. With 27 of 125 sessions (21.6%) one-way, the NDR cannot correlate request/response, misses C2, lateral movement and data exfiltration detections and generates incomplete session records.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR port using bidirectional 5-tuple hashing at the packet broker so the NDR sees complete sessions.

findings.root_cause: 91.0% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC), just above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is not being decrypted or enriched before the NDR, so payload is opaque to deep packet inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for signature and behavioral analysis. At 90.7% encrypted, the tool is largely blind to application content, reducing detection coverage to metadata/flow analysis only and missing payload-based threats.

recommended_fix.why: Advise selective TLS decryption or provide decrypted copy / enriched metadata from packet broker to restore payload visibility while staying below the NDR's 90% encrypted tolerance; if decryption not possible, tune NDR to focus on metadata analytics for encrypted flows.
